name: Cloud Security Assessment
description: Assessment of a cloud environment: identity, network, data and workload configuration.

sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.guidance: Written for a decision maker. Every statement here must be supported by detail elsewhere in the report.

questions.label: What was assessed, and why?
questions.help: One or two sentences a non-technical reader can follow. Name the system or environment and the reason the work was requested.
questions.placeholder: Describe the target and the business reason for the assessment.

questions.label: What is the overall result?
questions.help: State the headline outcome in plain language. Do not introduce findings that are not recorded elsewhere in the report.

questions.label: What are the most important risks to act on?
questions.help: Summarise the highest-severity findings. Leave blank if there are none; do not invent risks to fill the section.

questions.label: What should happen next?
questions.help: The one to three actions the reader should take away.

questions.label: What was in scope?
questions.help: List systems, networks, applications, accounts or cloud subscriptions that were covered.

questions.label: What was explicitly out of scope?
questions.help: Anything deliberately excluded. This protects both parties later.

questions.label: What limited the work?
questions.help: Time windows, credentials not provided, systems unavailable, testing restrictions. Say so plainly - unstated limitations become disputed findings.

questions.label: What were the objectives?
questions.help: What the work set out to determine or demonstrate.

questions.label: How was success measured?
questions.help: The criteria used to judge whether the objectives were met.

questions.label: Which providers, accounts and regions are covered?
questions.help: Name accounts, subscriptions or projects and the regions in use.

questions.label: How is the environment structured?
questions.help: Landing zone, organisational units, network layout, shared services.

questions.label: How is identity and access managed?
questions.help: Federation, roles, privileged access, service principals.

questions.label: Accounts and resources in scope
questions.help: One row per account, subscription, project or managed service assessed. Record the identifier a reader could look up, not a friendly nickname.

questions.label: How was the work carried out?
questions.help: Phases, techniques and the order they were performed in.

questions.label: What standards or frameworks were followed?
questions.help: For example the CIS Benchmarks for the provider, the provider's own well-architected security pillar, or NIST SP 800-53 mappings.

questions.label: What tools were used?
questions.help: Name the tools and versions where the version matters.

questions.label: Tooling used
questions.help: The tools the work actually relied on, with versions. A finding is only reproducible if the reader knows what produced it.

sections.title: Findings
sections.guidance: Misconfigurations, excessive permissions, exposure and gaps against the chosen baseline.

questions.label: What is the overall risk position?
questions.help: Interpret the findings as a whole. Severity of individual findings is set on each finding, not here.

questions.label: What is the business exposure?
questions.help: Consequences in operational terms: downtime, data exposure, regulatory obligations, cost.

questions.label: What assumptions underpin this analysis?
questions.help: State them, so a reader can challenge them.

questions.label: What should be fixed first?
questions.help: Ordered remediation. Reference findings by their identifier.

questions.label: What effort or dependencies are involved?
questions.help: Anything that affects sequencing: change windows, vendor involvement, cost.

questions.label: How will fixes be verified?
questions.help: Retest plan, acceptance criteria, who confirms.

questions.label: What longer-term changes are recommended?
questions.help: Improvements beyond fixing individual findings: process, monitoring, architecture, training.

questions.label: What can be improved immediately?
questions.help: Low-effort changes worth making now.

questions.label: What is the conclusion?
questions.help: Close the report. Do not introduce new facts here.

sections.title: Evidence
sections.guidance: Evidence attached to this report is listed with its reference, original filename and SHA-256 so a reader can verify it independently.

questions.label: Anything else the reader needs?
questions.help: Supporting detail, raw output references, glossary, contact information.
